analysis.body:
# AI Data Center Power and Grid Interconnection, September 2026

The US grid interconnection queues as of mid-September show 8,380 generation and storage projects totaling 1.33 million megawatts waiting to connect across ERCOT, NYISO, MISO, Southwest Power Pool, and CAISO. ERCOT alone accounts for 438,086 MW across 1,778 projects, dominated by solar (150,347 MW) and battery storage (159,820 MW), with natural gas at 78,092 MW. This queue composition—heavy on storage and renewables paired with significant gas capacity—reflects the infrastructure buildout required to serve large new load centers, including data centers, whose electricity draws must be matched by both generation and grid-scale batteries to maintain reliability around the clock.

Commercial-sector electricity sales across eight major states totaled 54.8 million megawatt-hours in June 2026, with Texas accounting for 15,754 MWh at the lowest price of 8.66 cents per kilowatt-hour, followed by California at 10,025 MWh at the highest price of 27.33 cents per kilowatt-hour. These figures capture the commercial class into which data centers are billed, though they represent a proxy for data center load rather than a direct measurement; the variation in pricing and volume reflects both regional generation mix and transmission congestion. Georgia, Virginia, and Ohio each showed 5,500–7,700 MWh of commercial sales at mid-tier prices, positioning them as emerging load-growth regions.

Storage capacity in the interconnection queues—159,820 MW in ERCOT, 67,027 MW in MISO, 52,913 MW in Southwest Power Pool, and 46,940 MW in CAISO—totals approximately 367,700 MW and represents one of the clearest signals of anticipated high-load growth, since battery projects are typically co-sited or networked with data center clusters to handle their continuous consumption patterns. Watch for queue movement velocity and commercial sales growth in Virginia and the Midwest through the next four quarters, as these regions show both rising interconnection activity and expanding load bases.
